I computed these from the raw BTS July 2025 file, so the figures are official DOT/BTS data.

**SFO departures, July 2025 (flights that actually departed)**

| Carrier | Departures counted | Avg departure delay (min) | Share delayed >15 min | Share delayed ≥15 min (BTS's own metric) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| United (UA) | 5,059 | 12.7 | 20.5% | 21.3% |
| Alaska (AS) | 1,020 | 10.6 | 21.5% | 22.1% |
| Delta (DL) | 1,224 | 14.0 | 23.6% | 24.3% |
| Southwest (WN) | 700 | 21.9 | 37.9% | 39.7% |

**Source**
- **File:** BTS TranStats, "Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance (1987–present)", July 2025 monthly file. I downloaded it from `https://transtats.bts.gov/PREZIP/On_Time_Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_1987_present_2025_7.zip`. The file is dated 14 Oct 2025.
- **Filter:** `Origin = SFO`, with `Reporting_Airline` set to UA, AS, DL or WN.
- **Average delay:** the mean of `DepDelay` over flights that have a departure delay value. Early departures count as negative minutes, which is BTS's convention. Cancelled flights have no value and are excluded. Diverted flights are excluded only if they have no value.
- **Share delayed:** flights with `DepDelay` above 15, divided by the same flights.

**Things to know before the slide**
- **">15" vs "≥15":** BTS's own on-time flag (`DepDel15`) counts 15 minutes or more. My ">15" column is the strict reading of what you asked. I included the BTS-flag version so you can match BTS's published tables. Use one consistently and label it.
- **Early departures:** if you count early departures as zero minutes late instead of negative, the averages rise to UA 15.7, AS 13.7, DL 17.2 and WN 22.8.
- **Mainline only:** these are the carriers' own reported flights.
  - United flights flown by SkyWest appear under OO, which was 2,957 SFO departures. They are not in the UA row.
  - Alaska's row covers AS only. No separate Horizon (QX) flights appear at SFO in this file.
  - Say "mainline" on the slide, or ask me to add the regional partners.
- **Schedule counts:** the scheduled counts, including cancellations, are UA 5,112, AS 1,041, DL 1,233 and WN 704.

I computed these myself from the official BTS raw file for July 2025. All four carriers' SFO departures come from that one file.

| Carrier | Scheduled departures | Cancelled | Avg departure delay (min) | Share delayed ≥15 min | Share delayed >15 min |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| United (UA) | 5,112 | 56 | **12.7** | **21.3%** | 20.5% |
| Alaska (AS) | 1,041 | 22 | **10.6** | **22.1%** | 21.5% |
| Delta (DL) | 1,233 | 9 | **14.0** | **24.3%** | 23.6% |
| Southwest (WN) | 704 | 5 | **21.9** | **39.7%** | 37.9% |

**Source:** the BTS/DOT "Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance (1987–present)" dataset, July 2025 file. Its table name is `T_ONTIME_REPORTING`. The download URL was `https://transtats.bts.gov/PREZIP/On_Time_Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_1987_present_2025_7.zip`. The dataset's landing page is `transtats.bts.gov`, under Aviation → Airline On-Time Performance Data.

**Method:**
- **Filter:** I kept rows with `Origin = SFO` and grouped by `Reporting_Airline` (UA, AS, DL, WN).
- **Average:** the mean of `DepDelay` over flights with a recorded departure delay. Cancelled flights are excluded. Early departures count as negative minutes, which is BTS's convention.
- **Share delayed:** flights with `DepDelay` of at least 15 minutes, divided by flights with a recorded departure delay.

**Caveats for the slide:**
- **15-minute threshold:** BTS and DOT define "delayed" as 15 minutes or more, so I'd use the "≥15 min" column. The "more than 15" column is there in case you want the literal reading. The difference is under 2 points for every carrier.
- **Regional flights are excluded:** BTS reports regional carriers under their own codes. SkyWest (OO) flies a lot of SFO departures for United, Delta and Alaska, and it isn't included in the United, Delta or Alaska rows. That means United's row is mainline only. If you want "United at SFO" as passengers experience it, say the figures are mainline only. SkyWest alone was 20.6 min on 2,951 flights, with an average delay of 10.6 min.
- **Sample size:** Southwest and Alaska have far fewer SFO departures than United, so their figures swing more with a few bad days.

Caveats:
- **LA:** The years 2016–2026 are separate datasets (for example, 2017 is `eq98-9f8w`, 2024 is `b7dx-7gc3`, and 2025 is `h73f-gn57`). I only read part of the portal's catalog listing, so there may be an older MyLA311 year that I missed. The 2016 dataset is the earliest I confirmed.
- **Houston:** The ArcGIS archive layer (`311_ARCHIVED_CASES`, 2011–April 2024) and its recent-requests layer were returning 500 "service not started" errors. I took the closure field from the header of the 2026 year-to-date file. The 311 page itself gives no column descriptions.
- **Philadelphia:** I got the field name from a live query against the Carto API. The OpenDataPhilly page doesn't list fields.
- **SF:** `updated_datetime` also holds the closure date for closed requests, but `closed_date` is the dedicated field.
